notes: Each inputJson is a complete independent manifest, including negative vectors; no patch DSL or hidden defaults.
Success asserts canonicalJson and artifactDigest. Validation checks metadata only, never blob existence, digest bytes or actual size.
Required-field/object/unknown-key failures use OWA_INVALID_MANIFEST. Invalid scalar annotation values use OWA_INVALID_ANNOTATIONS.

expiresAt is null or a portable RFC3339 timestamp: valid Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD, T/t, hours 00-23, minutes and seconds 00-59, optional fraction with one or more digits, and mandatory Z/z or signed HH:MM offset (hours 00-23, minutes 00-59). Leap seconds are not supported.

Date-only, missing-zone and calendar-rollover strings previously accepted by runtime date parsing are schema-invalid and now explicitly reject with OWA_INVALID_EXPIRY; timestamps are validated without normalization.

New expiry success goldens were computed independently with Python json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(comma, colon), ensure_ascii=False) and hashlib.sha256 over UTF-8; these fixtures contain only string and integer leaves, with ASCII keys, so no floating-point serialization assumptions are involved.

manifest-binary64-boundary-annotations (issue #38) carries hard binary64 values in scalar annotations so the complete canonical manifest bytes and artifact digest depend on rule-5 number serialization at its boundaries; it was authored with the same independent exact verifier as the canonical-b64-* vectors.

Scalar annotations carrying hard binary64 boundaries: smallest subnormal, largest finite (and a token that rounds down to it), shortest-digit ties resolved to an even final digit, the binary64 neighbours of the 1e-6 and 1e21 layout thresholds, 2^63, negative zero and negative underflow (both 0), a parse tie at the exact midpoint 1 + 2^-53, 0.1 + 0.2, 1/3 and 10^23. The complete canonical manifest bytes and artifact digest are pinned; a serializer that differs in any digit, threshold or exponent spelling produces a different artifact identity.
